related_questions.question: Where can I get the FMM form?

text_blocks.snippet: You can obtain the FMM (Forma Migratoria Múltiple) form, also known as the Mexican Tourist Card, both online and at the border. If flying, the cost is often included in your airfare. If traveling by land, you can fill out the form at the National Immigration Institute (INM) office at the border crossing. You can also fill it out online through the official INM website, print it, and then have it stamped by INM officials at the border.

list.snippet: Visit the official INM website (https://www.inm.gob.mx/fmme/publico/solicitud.html) to access the online application form.
Complete the form and pay the fee (if applicable) with a credit or debit card.
You must get the printed form stamped by INM officials at the border within 30 days to validate it.
Locate the INM office at the border crossing.
Fill out the paper FMM form provided by INM.
Pay the fee at Banjercito, the bank located near the INM office.
Have the form stamped by an INM official to validate it.

list.title: Cost:
list.snippet: If you are staying in Mexico for more than 7 days, there is a fee for the FMM. If flying, this fee is often included in your ticket price.

list.title: Stamping:
list.snippet: Whether you obtain the FMM online or at the border, it must be stamped by INM officials at the port of entry to be valid.

list.title: Retention:
list.snippet: You must keep the stamped portion of the FMM (or the stamp in your passport) safe, as you will need to surrender it when you leave Mexico.

list.title: Exceptions:
list.snippet: Some airports may have a digital FMM process, and some countries may require a visa in addition to the FMM.
